state.goal: Choose a Python test runner for an API and browser regression suite
state.question: Which runner should integrate new API tests with the existing browser suite?
known_constraints: new tests must cover API behavior and browser workflows in one CI job
supported browsers must retain their coverage
evidence: Scenario TEST baseline: API tests are new; there is no existing Python unit-test suite to migrate, and CI can install either runner.
Scenario TEST baseline: browser regression tests already exist, but their runner, fixture interfaces, and browser matrix have not been inspected.
Scenario TEST baseline: integration work depends on whether existing browser lifecycle fixtures belong to pytest or unittest; either runner supports ordinary Python API assertions.
Playwright official Python documentation describes pytest browser fixtures and browser matrix options: https://playwright.dev/python/docs/test-runners

Scenario TEST confirmed: browser tests import pytest-playwright and use conftest.py fixtures for page, browser_context_args, and authenticated_page; CI runs the chromium/firefox/webkit matrix through pytest.

Scenario TEST confirmed: new API tests need the same authenticated_page and context lifecycle. Retaining these shared fixtures and the full browser matrix is required; no rewrite of browser fixture infrastructure is planned.

alternatives.name: Pytest with existing browser fixtures
alternatives.description: Run API and browser tests under pytest, using pytest-playwright fixtures when present.
advantages: browser matrix integration through the plugin

alternatives.name: Standard unittest runner
alternatives.description: Run new API and browser tests with python -m unittest; rewrite any pytest-specific fixture and matrix orchestration.
disadvantages: pytest fixtures are not injected by the unittest runner
plugin browser matrix would need new orchestration
